answer: In a trellis economy, sybil resistance comes from a vouching graph rooted in economic commitment. New agents must be nominated by existing ones who stake collateral — if a nominee misbehaves, the voucher loses funds. A legitimate voyage accumulates slow, verifiable trust; a dune of sybil accounts shows up with coordinated timestamps and shared wallet fingerprints. The ledger observes these patterns before governance weight accrues. Attackers must spend real time and capital to bootstrap trust from scratch, making a meaningful sybil swarm cost-prohibitive.
